query: Create a .gitignore for a new Maven-based Java 21 service developed in IntelliJ on macOS.
expected_behavior: Places a single .gitignore at the repo root, based on the bundled java.gitignore reference, trimmed to Maven
Covers secrets/local config (*.env, application-local.*, keystores, credentials*), build output (target/, *.class), IDE files, OS cruft, and logs/crash dumps
Keeps wrapper files trackable (negation for gradle-wrapper.jar where relevant; .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties stays committed)
Mentions the global excludes file option for per-developer OS/IDE cruft

query: git status in our repo shows target/, .idea/, and app.log tracked and modified, even though .gitignore lists all three patterns. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that .gitignore only affects untracked files — already-committed files stay tracked
Finds offenders with git ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude-standard rather than guessing paths
Un-tracks them with git rm --cached driven from that list, keeping working copies, then commits

query: A teammate accidentally committed application-prod.properties containing the production database password three commits ago. They plan to add it to .gitignore and git rm --cached it. Is that enough?
expected_behavior: States clearly that it is not enough — git rm --cached removes the file from the current commit only; the secret remains in history
Requires rotating the secret immediately as the primary fix
Recommends scrubbing history (git filter-repo or BFG) with coordinated force-push, plus the .gitignore pattern to prevent recurrence
